caption: Some weeks the stock costs more than my room. Is R9 400 even worth calling an income?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R9 400
p/m income
Living in Bethlehem
slides.body:
Female, 24
Single, no kids
Job: Runs a fruit & veg stall at the taxi rank
Net income: R9 400 p/m (a good month)

slides.title: Stock
slides.includes: Fruit, veg and packaging from the wholesale market
slides.body: I go three times a week. If I skip a trip the stall looks empty and people walk past it.

slides.title: Room rent
slides.body: Cheaper than town, but I lose an hour walking to the rank and back every day.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: What doesn't come off my own stall
slides.body: I eat my unsold stock most nights. Groceries are really just the things a stall can't sell you.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the wholesale market and back
slides.body: This is the cost of buying the stock, before I've sold a single tomato.

slides.title: Stokvel
slides.body: The one saving I never touch. Everything else gets renegotiated with myself first.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Airtime & data, funeral policy, toiletries, bank fees, family support
slides.body: None of these feel big on their own. Together they're a quarter of what the stall makes me.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R9 400. Most of that already turned into fruit and veg before I saw a rand of it.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I upload my bank statement to Beyond Horizon between market trips and it sorts every transaction for me.

No bank login needed.
